study_design: Longitudinal nested case-control study using stored serum samples
cohort_total_n_excerpt: We studied serum 25(OH)-vitamin D levels of 622 prostate cancer cases and 1,451 matched controls
reason: The abstract evaluates prostate cancer risk overall and does not analyze an aggressive, advanced, metastatic, high-grade, high-risk, or lethal incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: We studied serum 25(OH)-vitamin D levels of 622 prostate cancer cases and 1,451 matched controls and found that both low (</=19 nmol/l) and high (>/=80 nmol/l) 25(OH)-vitamin D serum concentrations are associated with higher prostate cancer risk.
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate concerns overall prostate cancer risk, with no aggressive-disease restriction stated.
